_comment: TASK_COMPLIANCE_DATA_TRUTH_V1 D1b/D4: classes of canonical sections deliberately left out of the retrieval index. Each class carries the measured reason for its decision; 'pending' means observed but not yet decided (D4 decides from measured recall and decoy behaviour — L12). A section left unindexed and uncovered by a decided class fails scripts/compliance/truth/data_integrity.py.

classes.reason: decided at D4 from measurement (L12): (1) evidence containment — 0 of the answer key's 189 evidence quotes live in RSAW sections, so exclusion cannot cost delivery; (2) including the 7,731 RSAW rows REDUCES dev governing recall@20 (2/24 -> 1/24, d4_coverage_report.json) — audit-worksheet rows displace governing text at the same topic; (3) RSAWs describe the evidence an auditor expects, not what the operator does — the operator corpus carries that, and where an RSAW question is asked the standard's own Measures examples (indexed, Tier 0) answer it. The store keeps them addressable; the index does not retrieve them.

reclassified at D2 (measured): the document holds NINE captures of 330 sections each; SEVEN revisions (2,310 sections) were already indexed, only the two newest captures (660) were never projected — re-capture duplication, not a deliberate exclusion. Default scope (is_superseded=0) carries exactly one governing copy of 330 either way, so D4 measures those 330 for recall and decoy behaviour without an exclusion decision. D4 measurement: dev governing recall identical with the default-scope glossary included vs excluded (2/24 @20 both, d4_glossary_report.json), 0 of 189 key evidence quotes are glossary text, and the term-query decoy's top hit is the glossary's own definition row (a correct answer to a definition query, not pollution) — the glossary stays indexed; its nine-capture duplication is a capture-policy fact that default scope already shields (only the governing revision's 330 rows are in scope; D6 hardens the clock).

decided at D4: all 68 internal sections with no unit_kind are short (span<120) rows already unprojected — they predate the current extractor and none is indexed; D3's built-in fragment/furniture rules cover their shapes for future captures. Recorded so the coverage check sees a decided class.

decided at D3, applying the task's own D7 eligibility rule (TOC sections are never evidence): the internal extractor emits each ToC page as TABLE_OF_CONTENTS; indexed, one carried an IMPLEMENTS edge to CIP-007-6 R2 Part 2.1 (F6) and its dotted-leader listing pollutes every lexical arm. DOCUMENT_CONTROL sections were also excluded at first and then RESTORED: the answer key cites an APPROVALS block as operator evidence (product:CIP-003-9:coverage_gap) — approval signatures are citable content, so the control-block class stays retrievable and its findability misses are accepted (measured: ~120 of 2,365).

classes._applies_note: NOT applied by class match: the plan and the integrity check apply the built-in dated-change-row shape (internal, <=500 chars, date + change verb). This entry records the decision and its reason.
classes.reason: decided at D3, applying the task's own D7 eligibility rule (document machinery is never evidence): a dated change entry (date + change verb, under 500 chars) under the operative role is a revision-log row from a headingless history table — the store extractor's cutoff needs the history heading, and documents without one leak these rows into the operative population. Measured: the largest unique-heading findability miss class (rows like '1.1 <operator name> — Added CIP-002 Visio flow chart process … 05/04/2016' competing with their own siblings). The store keeps them addressable; the index does not retrieve them. The ingest side (internal_corpus) classifies them REVISION_LOG for new captures.

classes._applies_note: NOT applied by class match (no kind/pattern constraints here): the plan applies the built-in rule (whole text == title, under 120 chars); the integrity check verifies the same rule from section metadata. This entry records the decision and its reason.
classes.reason: decided at D2, applying the task's own D7 eligibility rule (heading-only sections are never evidence): a section whose whole text is its own title under 120 chars is a heading-only fragment. Measured shadow: a 39-char '1.1.1 Personnel and training (CIP-004)' fragment scores 0.895 against the requirement's own sentence while the composed Part scores 0.60 — the fragment outranks the unit it duplicates. The parent document carries the content; the unit is the heading line.

decided at D4: all 68 internal sections with no unit_kind are short (span<120) rows already unprojected — they predate the current extractor and none is indexed; D3's built-in fragment/furniture rules cover their shapes for future captures. Recorded so the coverage check sees a decided class.
